title: Reject staged input changes after registered research replays
body:
## Summary

The registered research replay's final “Committed inputs remain unchanged” gate runs only `git diff --exit-code`, which compares the working tree with the index. If a replay stages a changed input, a deletion, or a newly added file, the gate currently exits successfully despite the checkout differing from the committed inputs.

Keep that worktree comparison and also run `git diff --cached --exit-code` against the commit. Both comparisons matter: replacing the existing command with `git diff HEAD` would accept a staged edit whose working bytes were subsequently restored to HEAD. Ordinary untracked replay outputs remain allowed.

The regression tests read the actual named workflow run step and execute it with fail-fast Bash in tiny real Git repositories. They cover clean and untracked-output controls, unstaged edits/deletions, staged edits/deletions/additions, and an index-only difference hidden by a restored working file. They run in the existing `test_research_*.py` onboarding suite.

## Test plan

- [x] Before the workflow change, the eight new tests have exactly three failures: staged edit, deletion, and addition incorrectly pass the gate. After the change all eight pass under CPython 3.12.14 and 3.11.6 on macOS arm64.
- [x] `python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_ci_drift.py' -v` — 8 passed.
- [x] `python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_matrix_batches.py' -v` — 5 passed, including actual planner CLI coverage and unchanged matrix boundaries.
- [x] `git diff --check` passes. A full-checkout search found neither changed path in registered `SOURCES.json` or `VERIFY.json` declarations.

The existing planner deliberately selects all **1,629 registered packages** when this shared workflow changes; this PR retains that routing and does not bypass or filter it. The bounded local checks above exercised planning and the Git gate only. No all-package mathematical replay, selected cold replay, or hosted CI success is claimed. This is an end-of-replay cleanliness check, not a sandbox or proof that inputs were never temporarily modified during execution.

## Scope and attribution

Based on canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. The reusable workflow was introduced by ywz65 in [PR #2505](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2505), head `a357942c5ee5ce88948c120a0a174bb7dd0c2d2a`, and retained in Douglas R. Colkitt's integration commit `e182f1a175b3e7635b1c7a66fdf6f1c4a40cf3bd`. This change closes the staged-file gap in its existing drift contract. [PR #2602](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2602) separately checks publication bytes, and [PR #3142](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3142) validates sparse planning manifests; neither supplies this post-replay CI gate.

Exact-topic overlap was checked against a fresh snapshot of 344 open PRs, 2,964 closed PRs and 2,453 Discussion records, including the current handoff hub. No equivalent fix was found; text search does not prove exclusivity. Only this reusable workflow and its new behavioral tests change. Frozen sources, replay commands, scientific artifacts and the selected result remain unchanged.

Prepared by roger-sato with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in implementation and independent agent review. Apache-2.0.
